Chapter 6: Act Three

The attic had never been so crowded, and Jo had never been so pleased about it.

Meg held the lantern. Beth held the script, which she had copied out twice so that nobody would have to share. Amy held her opinion of the costumes, firmly, and very nearly to herself.

“Act three,” Jo announced, “in which the villain is unmasked, the heroine is rescued, and nobody faints, because I am tired of fainting.”

Laurie, from the rafters, asked who would be playing the villain.

Four heads turned to look up at him, and the lantern swung, and the shadows on the slanted ceiling made a great many villains out of one surprised boy.
